title: FinFET Inspection - Haze Detection on Zeta-20
subtitle: Post-CMP Quality Validation for 14nm Node Manufacturing
author: Dr. Thomas Mueller

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Zeta-20 system to detect and classify Haze defects during post-cmp inspection at the 14nm technology node. The test is conducted at Hsinchu Fab 12 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 200mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Haze defects that are critical to yield at the 14nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Zeta-20 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Zeta-20
- Inspection Type: FinFET Inspection
- Target Defect: Haze
- Process Step: Post-CMP
- Wafer Size: 200mm
- Technology Node: 14nm
- Fab Location: Hsinchu Fab 12

This test case applies to all Zeta-20 systems deployed at Hsinchu Fab 12 for post-cmp monitoring in the 14nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Zeta-20
Software Version: v8.7.733
Recipe: FINFET_INSPECTION_14nm_POST_CMP
Illumination Mode: Brightfield
Scan Speed: Low (72 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 1.0μm
Edge Exclusion: 3mm
Sampling Plan: 9-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Zeta-20 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'FinFET Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Haze defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 14nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 78 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 93% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±0.8% for FinFET Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.99 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2025-02-24
Wafers Tested: 38
Total Defects Found: 2031
Defect Density: 646.49 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 7.7%
Capture Rate: 90.1%
Test Duration: 102 minutes
System Uptime: 97.4%

Result Classification: PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Zeta-20 demonstrated excellent performance in detecting Haze at the 14nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate exceeds the target threshold; recipe tuning is recommended.

d) Edge-zone defect detection showed improved performance compared to previous revision.

e) The defect review station correlation was within specification.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS: No corrective actions required. Test passed all acceptance criteria.
